metadata.explanation: Composes the original subscript task with italicizing the '—Soak up the Science' text in the title. Getter checks: (1) a run containing '2' in the Title paragraph has font.subscript=True, (2) a run containing 'Soak' in the Title paragraph has italic=True. Partial credit: 0.5 per sub-goal. llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements are fully covered: (1) subscript on '2' in the title H2O, and (2) italic on the '—Soak up the Science' portion of the title.
Getter correctly retrieves the docx file, locates the 'Title' style paragraph, and checks run.font.subscript and run.italic on the appropriate runs.
Metric correctly applies partial credit (0.5 per sub-goal), resulting in scores of 0.0, 0.5, or 1.0.
Metric correctly handles 'expected.type=rule' — does not incorrectly access 'expected.get("rules", ...)'; instead reads directly from result dict.
Negative control resistance is sound: initial state (no subscript, no italic) yields score 0.0.
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before verification, ensuring the getter reads the latest on-disk state.

Minor concern: 'Soak' substring check is case-sensitive. If the title text is stored as all-caps 'SOAK UP THE SCIENCE' in the XML, the check would fail. However, the instruction quotes 'Soak up the Science' in mixed case, indicating the underlying text is mixed case (displayed uppercase via style), so the check should work correctly at runtime.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional robustness improvement: use case-insensitive check ('soak' in run.text.lower()) to guard against unexpected all-caps storage in the docx XML.
